questions.problem: The point $Q$ with coordinates $(-1,1)$ lies on the curve $y=f(x)$ and the point $R$ with coordinates $(-1,-2)$ lies on the curve $y=g(x).$ If the curve $y=g(x)$ is related to $y=f(x)$ via the transformation $g(x)=f(x)+k$, then what is the value of $k?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the point $R(-1,-2)$ lies $3$ units below the point $Q(-1,1).$ So, the graph of $y=g(x)$ can be obtained from the graph of $y=f(x)$ by shifting it $3$ units down. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14228870/assets/7d470919b374a5796b49ff81f893f37f5bb76afd4546a25459259f3b6339529b.png)

As a result, $k=-3.$

questions.problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(2,-1)$ lies on the curve $y=f(x)-3.$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=f(x)+1?$
questions.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The graph of $y=f(x)+1$ is obtained by translating the graph of $y=f(x)-3$ by $4$ units *up.* 

Hence, if the point $(2,-1)$ lies on $y=f(x)-3$, then the point 

$$
(2,-1+4)=(2,3)
$$

lies on $y=f(x)+1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14228870/assets/468f1e720d1a4834f1547b0cd2fcb8c9bff1e0342d2d98e33a62bbf9d473701a.png)

**Method 2**

As $(2,-1)$ lies on $y=f(x)-3$, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2)-3 & =-1 \\ f(2) & =-1+3 \\ f(2) & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if $x=2$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =f(2)+1 \\  & =2+1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the point $(2,3)$ must lie on $y=f(x)+1.$
